questions.q: How does Run Python Script (this lesson) differ from Get Data → Python script (Lesson 8)?
options: Get Data → Python script makes Python the entire data source; Run Python Script is a single transform step applied to data already loaded from somewhere else
They are two names for the exact same feature
Run Python Script can only be used with CSV files
Get Data → Python script only works inside Power Query Editor
questions.explain: These are genuinely two different integration points — one replaces the data source entirely, the other sits as one step inside an existing query pipeline.

questions.q: Where is the Run Python Script button located?
options: In Power Query Editor, on the Transform tab
In the Power BI service only, never in Desktop
In the Visualizations pane
Under File → Options and settings
questions.explain: It's a transform step, so it lives on the Transform tab inside Power Query Editor — reached via Home → Transform data first.

questions.q: What is the 'dataset' variable in a Run Python Script step?
options: The Power Query table already loaded into the script automatically — you never write code to create it yourself
A variable you must manually import using pandas.read_csv()
A reference to every table in the entire Power BI file
An empty placeholder that must be filled in before the script runs
questions.explain: dataset arrives pre-loaded with the query's current data — the defining feature that distinguishes this from Get Data → Python script, where you write the data-loading code yourself.

questions.q: What warning appears after running a Python script step in Power Query Editor, and why?
options: A data-privacy warning, because a Python script step counts as an external transformation requiring all data sources to have their privacy level set to Public
A warning that Python is not installed
An error stating the script contains invalid syntax
No warning appears under any circumstances
questions.explain: This privacy warning is expected and required — every data source touched by a query with a Python step needs Public privacy level for the script to work later in the Power BI service.

questions.q: What does the example script (using fillna with method='backfill') actually accomplish?
options: Fills missing values using a predictive method — pulling from the next valid value — rather than a flat default, and adds the result as a new column
Deletes every row containing a missing value
Converts all missing values to the text 'NULL'
Removes the dataset variable entirely
questions.explain: Backfill is a genuine predictive approach to filling gaps (using the next valid value), demonstrating something more sophisticated than a simple Power Query UI fill step could easily achieve.
